knowledge:
- key_parameters: sce=A SingleCellExperiment object containing log-normalized counts in the logcounts assay ;; dist=Distance or correlation matrix (defaults to weighted Spearman correlation with weights corresponding to gene variances) ;; nCeil=Maximum number of cells used to compute the range of top singular vectors (default 2000) ;; svdMaxRatio=Ratio determining the number of singular vectors used in clustering runs (default 0.08) ;; maxSets=Number of k-means clustering runs to create the consensus matrix (default 8) ;; k=Number of clusters, ideally matching the actual number of cell types. If not specified, estimated using the Tracy-Widom bound ;; consMin=Minimum consensus threshold (default 0.75) ;; kmMax=Maximum iterations for each k-means run (default 1000) ;; kmNStart=Number of times the k-means algorithm is repeated. Defaults to 1000 for N <= 2000 and 50 otherwise ;; fastSolver=Logical indicating whether to use a fast solver for dropout computation (default TRUE) ;; BPPARAM=Parallel execution parameter from BiocParallel (default bpparam())
- alternatives: None explicitly named; the documentation mentions "existing methods" generally and uses scater for preprocessing and mclust (adjustedRandIndex) for evaluation.
- when_to_use: Appropriate for scRNA-seq datasets with dropout events (where lowly expressed genes are recorded as zero) to improve downstream analyses like cell type classification and clustering.
- pitfalls: Input data must be pre-processed and log-normalized (accessible via logcounts(sce)) before running ccImpute, as the package does not perform preprocessing. With a high number of cells (N), imputation performance can drop due to increased noise if SVD parameters are not optimized (recommended: nCeil = 2000, svdMaxRatio = 0.08). K-means is sensitive to initial centroid choices; not setting kmNStart or setting it too low can lead to suboptimal results. Failing to specify k (number of clusters) relies on Tracy-Widom bound estimation, which should be reviewed for correctness.

workflows.name: standard_imputation
workflows.intent: Perform dropout imputation on a log-normalized SingleCellExperiment object using the high-level ccImpute wrapper.
input: sce (SingleCellExperiment object containing log-normalized counts in the logcounts assay)
workflows.stages: 1. Load required libraries ;; 2. Filter bad cells and remove unexpressed genes ;; 3. Recreate SingleCellExperiment and log-normalize counts ;; 4. Run ccImpute with parallel processing parameters to generate the imputed assay
workflows.code:
library(scRNAseq)
library(scater)
library(ccImpute)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(stats)
library(mclust)

sce <- UsoskinBrainData()
X <- cpm(sce)
labels <- colData(sce)$"Level 1"

#Filter bad cells
filt <- !grepl("Empty well", labels) &
        !grepl("NF outlier", labels) &
        !grepl("TH outlier", labels) &
        !grepl("NoN outlier", labels) &
        !grepl("NoN", labels) &
        !grepl("Central, unsolved", labels) &
        !grepl(">1 cell", labels) &
        !grepl("Medium", labels)
        
labels <-labels[filt]
X <- as.matrix(X[,filt])

#Remove genes that are not expressed in any cells:
X <- X[rowSums(X)>0,]

#Recreate the SingleCellExperiment and add log-transformed data:
ann <- data.frame(cell_id = labels)
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(normcounts = as.matrix(X)), 
                            colData = ann)
logcounts(sce) <- log(normcounts(sce) + 1)

library(BiocParallel)
BPPARAM = MulticoreParam(2)
sce <- ccImpute(sce, BPPARAM = BPPARAM)

workflows.name: decomposed_imputation
workflows.intent: Perform dropout imputation step-by-step using decomposed functions for finer control over distance calculation, SVD, clustering, and imputation.
input: sce (SingleCellExperiment object containing log-normalized counts in the logcounts assay)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate gene variances using rowVars_fast ;; 2. Compute the cell correlation matrix using getCorM ;; 3. Perform Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) using doSVD ;; 4. Run consensus k-means clustering using runKM ;; 5. Identify dropout events using findDropouts ;; 6. Impute dropouts using computeDropouts and store the result in the "imputed" assay
workflows.code:
cores <- 2
BPPARAM = MulticoreParam(cores)

w <- rowVars_fast(logcounts(sce), cores)
corMat <- getCorM("spearman", logcounts(sce), w, cores)

v <- doSVD(corMat, svdMaxRatio=.08, nCeil=2000, nCores=cores)

consMtx <- runKM(logX, v, maxSets = 8, k, consMin=0.75, kmNStart, kmMax=1000,
                    BPPARAM=bpparam())

dropIds <- findDropouts(logX, consMtx)

iLogX <- computeDropouts(consMtx, logX, dropIds,
                            fastSolver=TRUE, nCores=cores)
assay(sce, "imputed") <- iLogX
